A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 21-page SAGE paper, including Appendices A–L. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison; the appendix pages are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original AppWorld evaluations of SAGE and an implemented GRPO baseline, together with ablations, training curves and task-execution analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons and appendix experiments in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: The skill-library agent, Sequential Rollout, Skill-integrated Reward, SFT initialization and SAGE optimization procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same AppWorld training and evaluation coverage, including Test-Normal, Test-Challenge and the retained retrieval scenarios. No dataset, domain or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same ReAct, LOOP and GRPO comparisons. Comparator membership also matches in the retrieval, reward, initialization and SFT-initialized GRPO experiments in Tables 3–5 and 7.

E3.justification: The model, data splits, completion and efficiency metrics, rollout settings, training budgets and checkpoint-selection procedures remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain the same skill-removal, retrieval, reward-design and initialization ablations, longer-task-chain experiment, skill-usage analyses and task-execution case studies. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both state that reported results average three evaluation runs using the same model and retain the same plus/minus uncertainty reporting. Run-count information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 1 reports SAGE Test-Normal results of 72.0 TGC, 60.7 SGC, 12.1 average steps and 1,475 average tokens in both versions.

T1.justification: The GRPO and SAGE objectives and reward formulations are unchanged, including the general task-chain formulation in Appendix B and alternative rewards in Appendix J. No formal reasoning or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims about self-improvement, skill reuse, task performance and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of skill usage, retrieval tradeoffs, expert-data initialization and longer-chain performance are unchanged. The limitation to AppWorld and proposed extension to other agent datasets are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-availability statement and a link to the amazon-science/SAGE GitHub repository in the abstract, absent from v1. This adds implementation-access information; existing technical and training details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier agent, skill-library and reinforcement-learning research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining wording and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The addition causes limited page reflow: Section 4.3 begins on page 7 instead of page 6, Table 2 moves lower on page 7, and the conclusion extends onto page 9. Figure content, table designs, captions and appendix layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new code link provides an explicit implementation access point absent from v1, modestly improving code discoverability and reproducibility information. Scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information but do not establish the repository's completeness or functionality.
